ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary federal AML/CFT legislation is the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184. Federal corporate beneficial-ownership requirements are principally under the Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, sections 2.1, 21.1 and 21.303, and the Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512. Quebec requirements are principally under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR, c. P-44.1, including beneficial-owner disclosure provisions, and the Business Corporations Act, CQLR, c. S-31.1. Quebec's register is administered by the Registraire des entreprises. Sanctions screening is also governed by the United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2, the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), S.C. 2017, c. 21.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all beneficial owners, directors, officers, authorized signatories, principal lenders, major counterparties, and controlling entities before incorporation and periodically thereafter. Screening must cover United Nations sanctions implemented in Canada, Canadian sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and related regulations, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, Canadian domestic politically exposed person and head-of-international-organization categories under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, applicable U.S. OFAC lists where U.S. nexus or bank policy exists, and relevant Canadian law-enforcement or regulatory adverse-media sources. Document identity resolution, false-positive disposition, source of wealth, source of funds, ownership control analysis, escalation, and enhanced due diligence. OFAC screening is not generally a standalone Canadian statutory requirement but is commonly imposed by U.S.-linked banks and payment providers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Quebec Registraire des entreprises online services (Registre des entreprises du Québec) for a Quebec corporation or Quebec registration; Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre for a federal corporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act. A NUANS or equivalent corporate-name search is ordinarily used for federal name preapproval and may be requested for provincial name analysis.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec corporation must comply with the Charter of the French Language, CQLR, c. C-11, including French-language requirements applicable to its legal name, public-facing business name, signage, contracts, and commercial communications. A French version of the name is generally required for Quebec operations, subject to statutory exceptions. The legal name must be distinctive, not confusingly similar to an existing name or trademark, not misleading, and not contrary to public order. Federal corporations may use English, French, or both official languages, but Quebec operations remain subject to Quebec language law. Non-Latin transliterations should be accompanied by an acceptable French or English legal form where required by the registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banking, trust, loan, deposit, credit union, caisse, insurance, insurer, securities, exchange, investment fund, and similar regulated-financial terms without required authorization

University, college, school, hospital, municipality, city, province, Canada, Quebec, Crown, royal, federal, national, and similar governmental or public-institution terms where use implies official status or requires consent

Cooperative, caisse populaire, pharmacy, transport, security, detective, engineering, architect, lawyer, notary, and other regulated-profession or regulated-industry terms where statutory approval is required
Words suggesting charitable, public, diplomatic, military, or law-enforcement status without legal entitlement
Names that are obscene, discriminatory, deceptive, misleading, contrary to law or public order, or confusingly similar to an existing corporate name or protected trademark
The terms Inc., Incorporated, Corp., Corporation, Limited, Ltée, and equivalent legal-form designations unless the entity is validly incorporated or registered to use them
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain written reasons for rejection and identify whether the issue concerns distinctiveness, language, legal-form wording, regulated terminology, consent, trademark conflict, or similarity. File a revised name application with supporting consent letters, translations, trademark analysis, and explanatory submissions. For Quebec filings, use the administrative review or correction process offered by the Registraire des entreprises and comply with its prescribed deadline. For federal filings, request reconsideration or respond through Corporations Canada's name preapproval process; a refusal may be challenged through the applicable Federal Court judicial-review route after available administrative remedies are addressed. Preserve the reservation before expiry, and submit a fresh reservation if the administrative review will exceed the reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office address in Quebec is mandatory for a Quebec corporation, and a federal corporation must maintain a registered office in the province specified in its articles. A virtual office may be accepted for statutory correspondence if it is a real service address, receives official notices, and is controlled by the corporation or its authorized agent. It is not sufficient by itself to demonstrate operational substance for refrigerated pharmaceutical warehousing. The business should maintain an accessible warehouse, lease or ownership evidence, temperature-control systems, validated monitoring, inventory and quality records, trained personnel, insurance, and regulatory permits. Pharmaceutical storage may require Health Canada authorization depending on activities, including importation, distribution, wholesaling, or handling of drugs, and may require municipal, fire, environmental, occupational-health, building, and Quebec pharmaceutical-regulatory approvals.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated medium-to-high operational risk: approximately 15% to 30% annual probability of an unannounced or short-notice physical inspection for a new refrigerated pharmaceutical warehousing operation, with materially higher probability following a licensing application, adverse complaint, temperature excursion, importation activity, product-quality event, or compliance deficiency. This is a risk estimate, not a statutory probability or official enforcement statistic.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 4-16 (incorporation), s. 100 (solvency test), s. 113 (director residency), s. 154 (registered office); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 9, 12-16, 28-30 (initial declaration and annual updating).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ), reachable through the virtual office at entreprises.quebec; if a federal CBCA incorporation were elected instead, Corporations Canada would issue the certificate but the Quebec enterprise register would still be maintained by the REQ.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Incorporation) filed electronically with the REQ, together with the Declaration initiale required under the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises; the REQ issues the Certificat de constitution.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account is required under the QBCA; the articles merely fix the authorized capital structure (e.g., 1,000,000 Class A shares). Issued shares must be paid in fair consideration, and the solvency test in s. 100 governs all share repurchases and distributions. For the target cold-storage venture, the first board resolution records the transfer of C$1,000 subscription proceeds into the corporate operating account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the corporation accepts the subscription of 1,000 Class A common shares at C$1.00 per share, and the Secretary is directed to issue the share certificates upon receipt of the subscribed capital of C$1,000. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office is fixed at 123 rue de la Logistique, Montreal (Quebec), and that the Registraire des entreprises is notified of that office. RESOLVED FURTHER that the following officers are appointed forthwith: Andre Tremblay as Chief Executive Officer and President; Marie-Claire Bergeron as Corporate Secretary and Treasurer, each to serve until removed by the Board. RESOLVED FINALLY that the bylaws of the corporation are hereby received and adopted effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - Centre de services aux entreprises (CIDREQ), supplemented by the Canadian Intellectual Property Office trademark database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a written distinctiveness search in the Registre des entreprises and the CIPO database to ensure the proposed corporate name is not confusingly similar. Submit Form CID-01 (name reservation request) electronically through entreprises.quebec and pay the CAD 50 fee by ACH Direct or Bank Wire. The reservation is valid for 120 days and must be incorporated into the articles before expiry. If a numbered corporation is elected, this step may be bypassed and an assumed business name (enseigne) can be reserved later.
required_dossiers: Copy of the distinctiveness search report or examination screenshots
Proof of payment of CAD 50 fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the REQ refuses a name for confusion, lodge a written objection with supporting trademark or common-law goodwill evidence within the 30-day response window, reserve an alternate legal element, or adopt a numbered name and register an assumed en seigne under the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - legal publicity and electronic filing division (REQ Portal), with notarized signatures for paper-based execution where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts constitutifs under s. 14 QBCA, including the corporate name, authorized capital structure, share transfer restrictions if any, list of first directors (a majority of whom must be resident Canadians under s. 113), and the registered office address situate in Quebec. Execute the articles electronically on the REQ portal or before a notary, file the articles together with the CAD 200 filing fee, and attach the name reservation certificate. The filing simultaneously triggers the initial enterprise registration process.
required_dossiers: Consent of first directors acting in that capacity, showing Canadian residency
Power of attorney or mandate of filing representative (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of breach or query, amend and resubmit the articles within the prescribed curing period (typically 45 days) without penalty; if the objection relates to director residency, substitute a resident Canadian director by written consent and file the revised list immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Enterprise Register Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Certificat de constitution and attestation d' immatriculation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval of the articles, the REQ issues the Certificate of Constitution, assigns the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), and opens the corporation's file in the Registre des entreprises. Within 60 days, file the Declaration initiale containing the personal particulars of each director, the address of the registered office, and the place where records are kept; this declaration is the legal-publicity prerequisite for asserting corporate acts against third parties.
required_dossiers: Certificat de constitution issued by the REQ
Declaration initiale containing director particulars and registered-office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a clerical omission or registration error appears, file an online rectificative declaration to cure the record. If opposability to third parties is affected, petition the competent court for a correction order under the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises; prompt rectification abates late-filing penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and First Board Resolution (Corporate Governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation convened by the incorporator; corporate secretary and external notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting within seven days after issuance of the certificate. The directors adopt Bylaw No. 1, accept the share-subscription described in the pro-forma resolution, fix the registered office at the attested address, appoint the Chief Executive Officer, Corporate Secretary and Treasurer, adopt the banking resolutions designating ACH Direct and Bank Wire as payment rails, and authorize issuance of share certificates. All minutes and registers are maintained in the statutory records book.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution (text set out above)
Model Bylaw No. 1 adopted under s. 94 QBCA
Officer acceptance forms and indemnity acknowledgements
Commercial bank account opening forms including ACH/wire mandates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director fails the eligibility or residency condition, the board replaces that director by ordinary resolution and records the appointment; if shares were issued without full payment, the board reclassifies the receivable or obtains a unanimous shareholder resolution, thereby ensuring compliance with the QBCA solvency and share-issue provisions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registry Declarations and Tax Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec; Revenu Quebec; Canada Revenue Agency via the Business Registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File with the REQ the mise a jour declarations reflecting the registered office and officer changes within 15 days, and calendarize the annual declaration due before June 30 each year. Register the corporation for federal GST/HST and corporate income tax with the CRA using the RC59 Business Registration form, and open the Revenu Quebec QST account and source-deductions account if payroll is anticipated. The capital subscription is funded into the corporate bank account, and the bank acceptance certificate is retained in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NEQ attestation
Investor-officer list confirming majority Canadian-resident directors
Bank certificate of account opening and funding of subscribed capital
RC59 (CRA) and Formulaire LM-1 (Revenu Quebec) registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ or a tax authority returns an error notice, the corporation resubmits with the missing supporting documentation; late filings are normalized through voluntary-disclosure relief (CRA VP-01 or Revenu Quebec DVP-01) where no assessed failure exists, and registry inaccuracies are corrected by an online rectificative declaration to the REQ.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada - Quality Compliance and Licensing Division (Drug Establishment Licence) in conjunction with the Ministere de l'Agriculture, des Pecheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ) for food-grade cold cells, the Regie du batiment du Quebec (RBQ) for refrigeration-plant mechanical and electrical permits, and the municipal fire marshal under the Fire Safety Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Drug Establishment Licence (DEL) under the Food and Drug Regulations, C.R.C. c. 870, C.01A.005, covering storage and distribution of temperature-controlled pharmaceuticals, together with an RBQ certificate of conformity for the ammonia refrigeration installation and, where applicable, a MAPAQ sanitary permit (permis de salubrite) for co-storage of food products.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP); federal oversight by Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No full BAPE environmental impact study is required for a standard cold-storage warehouse. A ministerial authorization under s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2) is triggered when the ammonia refrigerant inventory exceeds the 2,000 kg hazardous-substance threshold or when the installation creates a confined-emission source; otherwise the project proceeds under the Category III declaration regime after obtaining MELCCFP's written opinion on assujettissement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Ammonia refrigeration systems must satisfy CSA B52-19 and ASHRAE 15 pressure-vessel, ventilation and leak-detection standards, with emergency dump-tank containment and pH-neutralized relief discharge before any sewer release. HFC/HFO systems must comply with the Ozone-depleting Substances and Halocarbon Alternatives Regulations (SOR/98-355), including technician certification, leak-repair records and refrigerant-charge-size logs. Condenser wastewater must meet municipal sewer-use bylaws and the EQA s. 20 general prohibition against contaminating discharge; solid waste is source-separated and registered with RECYC-QUEBEC where organic overspill occurs.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Code (CQLR c. S-3.1, r. 1) conformity certificate issued by the local fire marshal covering rack sprinkler coverage, high-hazard occupancy classification, ammonia engine-room separation, exit corridors and emergency lighting. A structural engineer's certificate confirms floor live-load capacity for the designed pallet stacking heights. Workplace clearance includes registration and first-aid compliance with CNESST, a hazardous-energy control program for compressors and conveyors, fixed ammonia gas detection and 24/7 alarm monitoring linked to a centralized emergency response service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Agence du revenu du Canada) — GST/HST, federal corporate income tax and payroll; Revenu Québec (Agence du revenu du Québec) — Quebec Corporate Income Tax, QST, and Quebec payroll; Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-login-services.html) and Revenu Québec CLICS (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/online-services/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada, including through an enterprise in Quebec, must first obtain a federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or registering online through Business Registration Online (BRO). For Quebec, the same registration triggers the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and QST number through Revenu Québec if the business makes taxable supplies in Quebec. Foreign entities not resident in Canada that are required to file a Canadian income tax return must also obtain a BN for corporate income tax purposes and may need to register for GST/HST under the Excise Tax Act if they are engaged in a commercial activity in Canada and are not a 'small supplier' or if they are non-residents who exceed the registration threshold or request to register voluntarily. Revenu Québec registration is completed via the 'Registration Form for an Enterprise Doing Business in Quebec' (LM-101-V) or electronically in CLICS, and requires a Quebec business address, the federal BN, and a representative to be designated.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style 'check-the-box' election exists under Canadian federal or Quebec tax law. Canadian corporations are automatically taxed at the entity level under the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act (Quebec). Foreign entity classification is determined under CRA administrative policy by reference to the legal characteristics of the entity and its jurisdiction of formation. Available elections relevant to corporate reorganisation and tax planning include the s. 85 income tax rollover election for transfers of property to a corporation, the s. 86 share exchange election, the s. 93(1) election on dividends from a foreign affiliate, the s. 256(9) designation to deem a person to be related, and the Quebec provincial corresponding elections under the Taxation Act. Hybrid mismatch arrangements are addressed through the general anti-avoidance rule and the hybrid mismatch rules in s. 12.6(1) and related provisions enacted under the Budget Implementation Act, but there is no elective mechanism to override entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) — dual value-added tax system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies over any four consecutive calendar quarters for both GST/HST and QST; non-resident persons carrying on a commercial activity in Canada are subject to registration if they exceed the threshold, provided they have a permanent establishment or make supplies in Canada; a non-resident may also voluntarily register. For QST, Revenu Québec applies the same CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for businesses making taxable supplies in Quebec; once registered, GST/HST and QST numbers are mandatory on invoices.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not currently mandate real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, or digital stamping. The CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic documents provided they meet the prescribed information requirements under the Excise Tax Act and the QST regime, including seller identification, registration numbers, description, tax rates, and total amounts. The federal government has launched voluntary electronic invoicing interoperability pilots (e.g., Pan-Canadian e-invoicing specification) but no statutory API-based clearance obligation applies as of the current tax year. Revenu Québec does not operate a live fiscal data reporting portal; tax returns and registrations are filed through CLICS.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the GST/HST and QST regimes for qualifying exports of tangible personal property from Canada when the goods are delivered or shipped outside Canada to a non-resident person, or to a carrier for export before the goods are used in Canada. For supplies of services, including warehousing and logistics services provided in connection with goods destined for export, a 0% rate may apply if the supply is made to a non-resident person and the service is not rendered in respect of Canadian real property, or if the service relates directly to tangible personal property that is exported in the course of the supply. The service must be contemporaneously documented and the goods must actually leave Canada within a reasonable period to support zero-rating; cold-chain storage provided before export may be zero-rated where the warehousing service is supplied to a non-resident customer and the goods are for delivery outside Canada, though the storage itself must be clearly tied to an export transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A Form) filed with the Canada Border Services Agency
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical shipment from Canada to the foreign destination
Commercial Invoice and purchase order from the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate or sufficient foreign exchange / payment evidence (wire transfer, SWIFT or bank statement) showing settlement in foreign currency
Warehouse receipt or cold-chain inventory records showing the goods were held in Canada in transit and subsequently removed for export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to stringent CRA and Revenu Québec audit review. The normal reassessment period for GST/HST and QST is four years from the filing date, but is extended indefinitely in cases of misrepresentation, fraud, or neglect attributable to the taxpayer. Where export documentation is incomplete, the zero-rated treatment is denied, resulting in a clawback of the tax amount that should have been collected, plus interest, and penalties under s. 280 and s. 285 of the Excise Tax Act (i.e., the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the understated tax in respect of false statements or omissions) and under s. 79.1 of the Quebec Tax Administration Act. Gross-negligence penalties may apply without a separate fraud determination, and criminal prosecution may be initiated for wilful evasion under s. 327 of the Excise Tax Act or s. 96.1 of the Quebec Tax Administration Act. Although Canada does not impose a statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, CRA guidance and transfer-pricing audit practice expect that export proceeds are repatriated in a commercially reasonable period; a delay exceeding 180 days may be treated as a shareholder benefit, an indirect loan, or an unpaid balance under s. 15(2) of the Income Tax Act and the Quebec equivalent, leading to an additional tax assessment on the amount outstanding.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) with residual exchange-control authority held by the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act; OSFI supervises Schedule I chartered banks; the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) licenses and supervises Quebec-regulated financial institutions. Payments Canada operates the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS), the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS), and the emerging Real-Time Rail (RTR).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely floating and fully convertible; Canada maintains no general exchange-control legislation and accepts IMF Article VIII obligations for both current and capital account liberalization. Profit remittance is lawful through dividends, interest, royalties, management fees, or loan repayments; the material hurdle is fiscal: Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends (statutory 25%, typically treaty-reduced), possible Quebec/Federal transfer-pricing adjustments, and anti-avoidance rules (e.g., deemed shareholder benefits, thin capitalization under subsection 18(4)).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender, conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline in Canada. A Quebec cold-chain warehousing entity may retain USD-denominated receivables in foreign-currency bank accounts, convert when commercially advantageous, or apply natural-currency matching for supplier obligations without Bank of Canada approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Multi-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational CAD-USD Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-medium. A foreign digital EMI cannot operate a deposit-taking or clearing system in Canada without a federal Schedule I banking charter or provincial credit union licence; such EMIs may at most register as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC for foreign-exchange dealing and remittance and, as of the Retail Payment Activities Act regime, be authorized but non-deposit-taking payment service providers. Their rails are acceptable for API-driven disbursement routing and FX execution, but capital escrow and high-value trade settlement should remain domiciled at a domestic Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical onboarding interview is generally mandatory for at least one director or an authorized signing officer at a Canadian branch of the chosen bank; remote/video opening is occasionally permitted for mid-market corporates with existing sponsor relationships and enhanced due diligence, but a newly incorporated Quebec entity with non-resident beneficial owners should anticipate an in-person visit, notarized corporate keys, REQ attestation, board resolutions, a specimen signature card, and a Canadian legal opinion on beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: De novo entity with no audited financial history handling high-value pharmaceutical inventory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry-certified articles of incorporation; Quebec Registraire des entreprises (REQ) attestation; opening balance sheet reviewed by a CPA; 24-month cash-flow projections; executed warehouse lease; CNA/GAP-equivalent pharma storage insurance; counterparty master services agreements; Canadian counsel legal opinion on ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) in a foreign jurisdiction triggering political-exposure or source-of-funds scrutiny
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate registry chart from ultimate parent to entity; certified passports; source-of-funds statements with supporting asset sale or financing documentation; negative adverse-media search; signed declarations from each 25%+ UBO; OSFI-compliant risk-rating questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentrated foreign receivables or third-party payment clustering from overseas pharma buyers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with named wholesalers; commercial invoices and packing lists; delivery temperature-log trail (IoT sensor reports) supporting trade substance; beneficiary whitelist; monthly treasury reconciliation mapped to ISIC 5210 commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected layering via frequent wire splits or unexplained large scheduled disbursements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution prohibiting cash payments and mandating ACH/Direct or wire rails; full disbursement ledger with purpose codes; accountant negative-confirmation; invoice-level support for each five-figure transaction; pre-approval protocol for disbursements above materiality threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 wire in CAD or USD to the Canadian operational account with remittance information citing the transaction nature (e.g., equity subscription, shareholder loan, or intercompany advance) and the ISIC 5210 cold-storage commercial purpose. Equity subscriptions require updated minute book, share register entries and an REQ return; shareholder loans require a contemporaneous written agreement, arm's-length interest rate consistent with CRA transfer-pricing rules, and tax reporting elections (e.g., thin capitalization position). All CAD domestic railings settle through LVTS (real-time) or ACSS (ACH T+1); USD-denominated inbound wires clear through correspondent banking with a mid-value date risk assessment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct low-value wires and Commercial Documentary Credits (MT700 issuance, MT707 amendments, MT720 transfers) for high-value, time-sensitive import of refrigeration spares, insulation panels, and pharmaceutical cold-chain consumables. Domestic payroll, utilities, and lease rentals settle via ACSS ACH-Direct with Interac e-Retail for vendor disbursements under CAD 10,000; FX conversions for USD supplier liabilities are executed on a centralized spot position through the primary bank with LVTS settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for CAD exposures where deliverability is contractually constrained, offered by authorized Schedule I banks
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and long-term cross-currency interest rate swaps) for matched-asset treasury positions
Vanilla CAD/USD options and collar structures under an executed ISDA/CSA master agreement
Natural-currency offset through foreign-currency deposits (no hedge ratio restriction)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is not statutorily penalized with a financial fine, but persistent non-filing may lead to administrative dissolution by Corporations Canada, resulting in loss of legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration under Quebec's An Act respecting legal publicity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary of the date of registration of the enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual declaration within the prescribed period may result in administrative strike-off from the Register, administrative penalties, and prohibition against carrying on activities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the corporation's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, interest charges, and potential criminal sanctions for willful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Corporate Income Tax Return (CO-17) and Annual Information Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the corporation's taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties, interest on unpaid amounts, and possible suspension or cancellation of the corporation's registration upon continuous default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is compulsory for distributing corporations, federal corporations subject to the CBCA where shareholders do not unanimously waive the auditor requirement, and Quebec corporations that are reporting issuers or where the requisite shareholder consent arriving at an audit waiver has not been obtained. No revenue-based numeric threshold applies generally to private CBCA/QBCA corporations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is mandatory for Canadian public corporations; private enterprises may elect either IFRS or the Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), which is the applicable local GAAP for most private cold-storage warehousing corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law requires every corporation to maintain a register of individuals with significant control, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec must be notified annually of any updated beneficial ownership information included in the annual declaration. Any change in significant-control holdings involving share transfers must be recorded and reported to the REQ within the statutorily prescribed update window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (UBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 120 to CAD 500 (approx USD 90 to USD 375) per year
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 5,000 to CAD 15,000 (approx USD 3,700 to USD 11,200) for a standalone private cold-storage logistics entity
